decisions.reason: The source changes only the Title style font size; it does not change bullet sizing, alignment, balance, or the bullet design reference.
The Title style font-size change does not alter Tab-based sublevel creation or list-hierarchy alignment.
Changing the Title style to 28 pt does not alter the required PBU naming prefix or its applicability.

The deployment requirement already requires consistent application of the prescribed style system; the Title typography value is owned by the source Requirement and does not change that deployment rule.
The source changes the Title style font size and does not affect numbered-list alignment at double-digit values.
The Title style font-size decision does not change the templates' default language configuration.
The source specifies Title typography but does not change any expected legacy copy-paste layout or style-stability behavior.
The Title font-size change does not modify the supported Word environment or the requirement for stable rendering across users.
The source does not address pasted tables, column containment, or the unresolved feasibility conflict for table adjustment.
The Title style font-size change does not affect users' ability to create manual line breaks after pasted content.
The source changes the Title style size, not the language used for style names or other template interface text.
